concern_details.detail: required runtime environments and software artifacts
concern_details.why: Java 23 JVM and MySQL server are shown as execution environments; the runtime artifacts (application classes, persistence.xml, hibernate-core 6.6.50.Final, mysql-connector-j 9.4.0, forms_rt 7.0.3) match pom.xml:34-52 and persistence.xml; the Maven/JDK 23 build environment and Maven Central are also shown for building in a new environment.

concern_details.detail: where the application runs and where its data is stored
concern_details.why: The Swing process runs in the JVM on the user workstation; the data is in schema reports_db in MySQL on the database host, labelled as 127.0.0.1 by default (persistence.xml:26-27).

concern_details.detail: how the main runtime elements communicate
concern_details.why: The chain app -> Hibernate (JPA) -> JDBC driver -> MySQL over TCP :3306 is shown with labelled relations; the code has no other network protocol.

concern_details.detail: technologies and runtime dependencies between the application and the database
concern_details.why: JPA/Hibernate, the MySQL JDBC driver, the persistence unit config, the port, the schema and user, and hbm2ddl.auto=update (with the note that the database and user must already exist) are all shown.

level_why: For a detailed deployment view, the diagram shows nodes, execution environments, versioned runtime artifacts, the config artifact, the port, the schema and user, and the schema-creation behaviour, without going down to classes. That is detailed deployment level, neither class level nor just boxes.

findings.claim: The JDBC-over-TCP connection is drawn as a dependency from an artifact to the MySQL execution environment, crossing node boundaries. In UML, network connectivity between nodes is a communication path (an association between nodes), not an artifact-to-node dependency.
findings.fix: Add a communication path between the JVM (or workstation) and the MySQL server labelled <<JDBC/TCP>> :3306, and keep jdbc -> mysql only as a usage dependency, or drop it.

findings.claim: The app ..> jvm <<deploy>> and schema ..> mysql <<deploy>> arrows repeat what nesting already says, and they point at the edge of the container that holds them. Using both notations at once is redundant.
findings.fix: Use nesting only and remove the two <<deploy>> arrows (inventory relations app->jvm and schema->mysql).

findings.claim: The 'loads forms' label suggests .form files are loaded at runtime. In fact the GUI classes call forms_rt layout classes (GridLayoutManager/GridConstraints) in code generated from the forms, and no .form file is read at runtime.
findings.fix: Relabel as '<<use>> GUI layout classes' (or similar).

findings.claim: The inventory evidence for app -> pxml cites JpaUtil.java:15, which is a field declaration. The persistence unit is actually loaded at line 17.

The database host is drawn as a separate device. The README's setup grants reports_user only @'localhost' and the JDBC URL is 127.0.0.1, so as configured MySQL must run on the workstation. A DevOps reader could assume a remote DB works without changes.
findings.fix: Extend the dbhost label or the schema note: a separate host needs a changed JDBC URL and a MySQL user granted for the client host.

findings.claim: 'Application classes' is a set of packages, not a deployable file. No packaging (jar) is defined in the pom, which the README notes, but the diagram does not show that this is unknown.
findings.fix: Name the artifact for its build output (e.g. target/classes, municipal-report-management-1.0-SNAPSHOT) and note that packaging is not defined.
